text: We tested temperature-scaling of the weak supervisor's soft targets, with a target temperature of 0.5, in a weak-to-strong setup pairing a qwen2.5-0.5b supervisor with a qwen2.5-7b student. The weak supervisor reached 0.47 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.87, while the strong student trained on the scaled weak targets reached a transfer accuracy of 0.69 with a standard error of 0.06. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.54, with a standard error of 0.16, against a baseline PGR of 0.48. This difference falls well within two standard errors of the baseline, so the data do not support a claim that temperature scaling helps; the observed ordering is compatible with noise. An important caveat is that the experiment used only num_seeds = 2, which makes the standard error estimates themselves fragile. Further seeds would be needed before drawing any directional conclusion about this intervention.
